newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Guam likely to renew fuel oil, seeks diesel deal.
newsitem.headline: Guam likely to renew fuel oil, seeks diesel deal.

text.p: Guam Power Authority (GPA) is likely to renew its one-year fuel oil term purchase contract with Daxin Petroleum Pte Ltd starting in August when the current deal expires end-July, its general manager said on Thursday.
The new contract will run from August this year to July 1998 after the current agreement expires on July 31.

Randy Wiegand said GPA also plans to issue a purchase tender in July or August for a new annual diesel contract to supply one of three independent power producers on the island situtated in the Pacific Ocean.
Wiegand said he would recommend the GPA board to renew the fuel oil contract for another year.
"Initial indications from Daxin are that they are willing to extend for another year under the same terms," he said.
Under the existing deal, GPA buys 2.7 million barrels of 2.0 percent sulphur fuel oil and 300,000 barrels of the 1.19 percent sulphur grade.
GPA plans to raise the volume of 2.0 percent sulphur fuel oil imports under the proposed extended contract with Daxin to about 3.1 million barrels, Wiegand said.
Daxin sold the 2.0 percent sulphur fuel oil at a premium of $2.23 per barrel to Singapore spot quotes for 3.5 percent sulphur fuel oil, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Guam.
The 1.19 percent fuel oil grade was sold at $3.15 per barrel above the Singapore 3.5 percent sulphur quotes, c-and-f.
Wiegand said the new contract for 0.5 percent sulphur diesel, scheduled to start by the end of the year, would seek a minimum of 175,000 barrels and a maximum of 700,000 barrels annually.
The diesel would be supplied to a new 40 megawatt diesel-fired power station on the island, which is scheduled to start in September or October, he said.

He said GPA would also seek to renew existing annual term contracts for diesel with local affiliates of Royal Dutch Shell and Mobil Corp under the terms of the existing deal for October 1996-September 1997.
But the volume for the 1997-1998 contract and subsequent contracts would be lower as power stations have been raising the use of fuel oil for generation at the expense of diesel.
Under the current contract, Shell supplies 23.0 million gallons (548,000 barrels) and Mobil supplies 15.2 million gallons (361,000 barrels) of diesel.
Shell's contract was sealed at a premium of 7.94 cents per gallon to Singapore spot quotes, free-on-board (fob) basis while Mobil's was at 7.63 cents per gallon above Singapore spot quotes, fob.
